chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Billie Holiday's tragic image
summary: Ramirez and Dance on Billie's sad later image and the death-wish malaise they dislike in her cult.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: I'd say prior her image was dramatic. My personal image, when I saw her and all that, was more tragic. To me.
Well, it seems to me that a lot of people like her
They feel like sort of a drugged world...
It's sad. And she became a sad singer of song.

But beyond sadness which you can take, there's something a bit sordid about it, I feel. You know, it's repellent to me. It's like a lot of people sort of had... There was a period, I think here, where a lot of people seemed to sort of have a death wish or something! Well, Carter, when he spoke of a malaise, he used the right word. I think there was a malaise in this nation. And all that sort of Billie Holiday cult of the later years seemed to me to be part of it! I didn't like it.
